column10: 'The father of Keilah the Garmite' (1CH 4:19, אֲבִי קְעִילָה הַגַּרְמִי): in 1 Chronicles 2:42-55 and 4:1-23 'the father of' a name is the founder of a town (Mesha the father of Ziph, Hur the father of Bethlehem, Ashur the father of Tekoa, Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa, 2:42; 4:4-5, 17), and Keilah is the town of the lowland of Judah (JOS 15:44) that David saved from the Philistines (1SA 23:1-13); 'the Garmite' is said of the founder, since a town is no Garmite. No man Keilah is named; the Septuagint, the Vulgate and the Synodal read Garmi as a name of its own, which names no man Keilah either. The word already stands on the town keilah-2 in BHSA, Brenton's Greek and the Vulgate, and BibleData's person Keilah, made from this verse, is folded into it
